text: SpecDev Workbench 是面向 DSH Web 和 Desktop 的项目资料工作台。它通过侧栏入口打开工作区资料页，并把 Markdown 文档、工作流和生命周期图、源代码证据及历史快照组织在一起；用户还可在可漫游的 3D 房间里按业务浏览资料、调整环境并导出含所选资料的单文件房间。适合需要整理和展示项目设计资料、在房间中阅读或分享选定内容的 DSH 用户。需要 DSH 和 Git 项目工作区，可选配置 repoRoot；不要求额外 API Key。

SpecDev Workbench brings project documents, diagrams, and Git snapshots into DSH. Browse materials by business in walkable 3D rooms, then export selected materials as a standalone room. For DSH users who want to read or share project design materials. Requires DSH and a Git workspace; no API key.
我想在 DSH 里把项目文档和流程图按业务整理起来。
能不能在一个可漫游的房间里阅读项目资料？
想把选中的项目文档和图表打包成离线房间分享。
How can I browse project docs and workflow diagrams together inside DSH?
I want to share selected project materials as a standalone room.
SpecDev Workbench 的项目资料清单：打开工作区后按业务列出登记的文档和图表，并呈现图表快照状态。页面通过 inventory 接口读取清单。
SpecDev Workbench 的业务房间资料绑定：检查建筑蓝图中的房间与业务对应关系，并为房间整理可阅读的文档和图表目录。
SpecDev Workbench 的图表历史快照：检查工作区图表状态后，可将确认过的提交保存为 Git 附注标签快照，供之后查看历史版本。
SpecDev Workbench 的房间分享导出：选择业务资料、主题和亮度后生成单个 HTML 房间文件，供接收者离线浏览选定内容。
帮我把业务设计文档和流程图放进能探索的 3D 空间。
Can I turn registered project materials into a walkable room for review?
I need to save a chart version and revisit it later from the project workspace.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · SpecDev Workbench：A “business” here means one feature or subject in your project, such as sign-in or a reading list. Its registered materials can have an independent room.

**[Try the offline room](https://github.com/pioneer666-user/specdev-workbench/releases/download/v0.2.3/specdev-reading-list-0.2.3.html)** · **[Install the plugin](#install-the-plugin)**

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · SpecDev Workbench：Download the HTML file and open it in a browser; this is a file download, not a hosted demo. The room and selected documents/diagrams work offline. Source links still need a network connection and, for private repositories, access permission.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · What you can do：- **Understand a project.** Browse registered Markdown documents, interactive workflow and lifecycle diagrams, node explanations and pinned source evidence. The regular 2D reader remains useful for focused reading and historical snapshots.
- **Make a place for its materials.** Ask the bundled AI skills to arrange existing furniture using furnished layouts as a starting point. Choose forest or ceramic, browse twelve furniture models, and describe your preferences in ordinary language.
- **Read inside the room.** Walk to a bookshelf, desk or notice board to open its bound materials, or use the complete material list. Reading pauses walking; closing the reader returns you to browsing.
- **Set the atmosphere.** Adjust brightness, rain, wet reflections and sound. Quick controls and display/weather/sound settings stay in sync. Sound starts only when you enable it.
- **Share a room.** Export one HTML file containing the room and selected materials. Recipients can explore it without installing DSH or this plugin.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · What you can do：The skills are written instructions that help the AI use the plugin's formats and validation tools. They do not automatically turn source code into correct project documentation or guarantee that every AI model will produce an attractive room.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Install the plugin：You need **DSH installed and able to open a workspace** first. Start with the [official DSH project](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) and its [user documentation](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/). This plugin's room, reading and export experience has been verified on **Windows with DSH Desktop and Web 0.2.0-rc.2**; other hosts and platforms are not covered by that result.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Install the plugin：Current plugin version: **0.2.3** · [Release and checksums](https://github.com/pioneer666-user/specdev-workbench/releases/tag/v0.2.3) · [Exact npm version](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench/v/0.2.3)

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · First install: Windows Desktop：Open DSH once to finish its initial setup. Save your work and exit through its menu or tray; confirm the background instance has ended. Use that installation's bundled CLI. Keep the data root DSH already uses: if you never set `DSH_HOME`, leave it unset. You do not need to build the plugin from source.

Run this in PowerShell, replacing only the installation directory:

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · First install: Windows Desktop：~~~powershell
$DesktopDir = 'C:\Apps\DSH' # Replace with your actual DSH installation directory
& "$DesktopDir\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add '@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench@0.2.3' '--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/'
& "$DesktopDir\DeepSeek Harness.exe"
~~~

Open **SpecDev Workbench** in the sidebar. It appears in the central panel; **Return to chat** restores your conversation.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · First install: Web：Finish the host's initial setup, then stop the Web instance. Use its own `dsh` CLI and the same data root:

~~~sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench@0.2.3 --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
~~~

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · First install: Web：Restart that instance. The sidebar entry opens the workbench in a new tab, keeping the chat available. For hosts launched through npm or a source checkout, see the matching CLI invocation in the [installation guide](https://github.com/pioneer666-user/specdev-workbench/blob/main/docs/public/guide.md#installation-and-upgrades).

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Already installed?：Back up your custom plugin configuration and record the installed package name before upgrading. Use the matching Desktop/Web command above for the current npm identity. Reinstalling an already installed version can be skipped by the host; historical identities need separate migration care. Read [upgrades, local package installation and data roots](https://github.com/pioneer666-user/specdev-workbench/blob/main/docs/public/guide.md#installation-and-upgrades) before removing anything. Keep your existing project data.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：1. **Choose a Git project in DSH.** Select the repository root as the workspace, then select that project in SpecDev Workbench. If the list is empty, create a DSH workspace and refresh it. Materials are registered under `docs/specdev`; existing registered materials can go straight to step 3.
2. **Prepare and register a subject's materials.** In that project's chat, ask the AI to use **specdev-business**. Confirm the target repository, allowed branch and subject; provide requirements or existing documents. For example:

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：> Use specdev-business to prepare and register documentation and a workflow for a “Reading list” subject in the current Git project. The proposed feature lets a user add a book and mark it as read. Work only on design materials, without implementing the feature. Confirm the repository and allowed branch with me, and ask about unclear requirements. Validate the materials and give me the workbench entry to review.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：Replace this example with your own subject and requirements. The AI may need decisions before it can finish. Existing documents can remain at their original repository paths when registered; proposed designs must be marked as such.
3. **Ask for a room around those materials.** Once the materials are registered, say:

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：> Use specdev-room to create a forest room for the registered “Reading list” subject in this project. I want to read its existing materials there; arrange the rest for me. Use a furnished layout as a starting point, bind the real materials, and run the final complete room check.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：You can choose ceramic instead, specify furniture, or let the AI arrange it. The room skill writes the room configuration and validates it; it does not create new documents, diagrams or models.
4. **Open and explore.** Refresh the workbench, select the subject and enter its room. Inspect the overview, walk to a reading spot and open a material. You decide whether the arrangement looks and feels right.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Your first room：The [getting-started guide](https://github.com/pioneer666-user/specdev-workbench/blob/main/docs/public/guide.md) covers registration, controls, export, troubleshooting, migration and source builds. The bundled [specdev-building skill](skills/specdev-building/SKILL.md) also supports a whole-building overview and walking experience.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Compatibility and scope：Rooms support floor furniture and one level of tabletop objects, arranged through AI-edited configuration. In-page furniture editing, arbitrary scaling, wall mounting, nested supports, cross-room links and sitting animations are not available. Room validation checks placement and registered-material readability; diagram compilation has its own validator.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Compatibility and scope：Workflow and lifecycle diagrams are supported for authoring/registration. Sequence and other upstream diagram types are not exposed as project materials. Old workflow reading and snapshots remain compatible; old projects and graphs are not automatically migrated.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Compatibility and scope：Brightness, weather, sound and furniture visibility last only for the current page. Sound pauses in the background and requires manual resume. Exported rooms start sunny and silent; sharing includes selected materials, not the whole repository or its history. Review sensitive text before sharing. See the guide for full export limits and compatibility boundaries.

@pioneer_zmc/dsh-workbench README · Compatibility and scope：The current guides live on public **main**, added after the 0.2.3 release. The published 0.2.3 package and tag retain their original README files and do not contain these guides.
